correctness.rationale: Every fixed-common-richness subset comparison with at most four tips is exhausted by a constant-Jaccard case or a 12/3 split of quartet two-tip comparisons. Substitution of fixed-root descendant-edge indicators gives complete UniFrac multisets. Exact monotonicity and rational subtraction yield the positive-balanced iff inequality and strictly negative-pectinate margin; all denominators are positive on the domain. A shared-reference witness attains the bound. Independent exact rational edge recomputation passed for 2,262 four-tip branch profiles; it supplements rather than proves the unrestricted identity.

originality.rationale: The foundational metric definitions and existing broad phylogenetic-similarity comparisons do not imply the exact equal-richness minimal quartet theorem. Complete enumeration of the rooted quartet edge-presence signatures supplies a new if-and-only-if branching-age threshold and signed margin. Published published-finding corpus searches and both owned ledgers were compared by object and implication, not titles alone; an unindexed general weighted-Jaccard theorem is a residual risk.
residual_risks: Targeted search and full-text inspection cannot rule out an unindexed more general phylogenetic Jaccard tree-order theorem.
UniFrac is defined here on a fixed crown-rooted reference tree; rerooting, a common ancestral stem or different union convention may change both scores and comparability.
The finite rational verifier samples branch lengths only; correctness over all real fractions depends on the complete algebraic proof.

evidence: UniFrac normalizes the unique branch length between two community sets by branch length present in their union.

value.rationale: This is the first possible species-pool size under matched richness and a necessary-and-sufficient branch-age and tree-shape criterion, not a selected anecdotal counterexample. It quantifies the maximal offending phylogenetic margin and demonstrates three-community common-reference attainability. It isolates a motivated finite-boundary issue in ecological beta diversity and separates taxonomy-driven and phylogeny-driven ordering.
